claims.claim: **Pelvic fractures are high-energy injuries, usually with multiple other injuries, and can bleed massively into the pelvis causing shock.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Trauma - Pelvic injury' (Last updated March 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Trauma_-_Pelvic_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: Pelvic fractures are **rare in children** and usually follow a high-energy mechanism; they can come with **life-threatening injuries elsewhere — intracranial, thoracic, abdominal, spinal and genitourinary.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Trauma - Pelvic injury' (Last updated March 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Trauma_-_Pelvic_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Pelvic bleeding is mainly venous and often retroperitoneal** — hidden, so keep a high index of suspicion.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Trauma - Pelvic injury' (Last updated March 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Trauma_-_Pelvic_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **High-risk mechanisms:** crush injury · motor vehicle collision (especially ejection, lateral impact, rollover or a fatality in the same collision) · pedestrian or cyclist vs car · fall from height (typically over 3 m) · heavy object falling onto the child (e.g. horse, quad bike).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Trauma - Pelvic injury' (Last updated March 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Trauma_-_Pelvic_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Haemodynamic compromise:** tachycardia (bradycardia is late), hypotension, prolonged capillary refill, end-organ hypoperfusion such as GCS under 15.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Trauma - Pelvic injury' (Last updated March 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Trauma_-_Pelvic_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Signs of pelvic injury:** bruising, wounds, asymmetry or deformity of abdomen, pelvis or legs; tenderness over the pubic symphysis, iliac crests, ischial tuberosities, sacroiliac joints or lumbosacral spine; blood at the urethral meatus, vaginal or rectal bleeding, scrotal bruising.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Trauma - Pelvic injury' (Last updated March 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Trauma_-_Pelvic_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Test stability once only, by gentle iliac-crest compression, ideally by the most senior clinician** — skip it if instability is obvious or pelvic CT/X-ray is already planned. **Never 'spring' or rock the pelvis**; it can increase bleeding.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Trauma - Pelvic injury' (Last updated March 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Trauma_-_Pelvic_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Log roll with caution — defer it if it risks worsening an unstable pelvis.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Trauma - Pelvic injury' (Last updated March 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Trauma_-_Pelvic_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Suspected unstable pelvic fracture: manual stabilisation while a pelvic binder is placed urgently.** Resuscitate if haemodynamically unstable.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Trauma - Pelvic injury' (Last updated March 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Trauma_-_Pelvic_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **If a binder is indicated, apply it before intubation**, and have one ready in advance when the mechanism and pre-hospital findings suggest pelvic injury.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Trauma - Pelvic injury' (Last updated March 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Trauma_-_Pelvic_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Apply at the level of the greater trochanters.** Too high (over the iliac crests) it won't work and may worsen the injury.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Trauma - Pelvic injury' (Last updated March 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Trauma_-_Pelvic_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **No proprietary binder is clearly better.** If the available binders are too big for the child, use a sheet.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Trauma - Pelvic injury' (Last updated March 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Trauma_-_Pelvic_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Where the lower limbs are not fractured, tie the feet together** — a figure-of-eight bandage or sling round the ankles — this internally rotates the hips and may help tamponade pelvic bleeding.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Trauma - Pelvic injury' (Last updated March 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Trauma_-_Pelvic_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Sheet method:** folded sheet under the child at the greater trochanters, ends crossed and twisted over the pubic symphysis, pulled firmly by two team members; secure with clamps — **plastic rather than metal**, which can obscure X-ray and CT.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Trauma - Pelvic injury' (Last updated March 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Trauma_-_Pelvic_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **AP pelvic X-ray.** FAST is controversial and of limited use for pelvic fractures — **don't delay the binder to do FAST.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Trauma - Pelvic injury' (Last updated March 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Trauma_-_Pelvic_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **No haemodynamic improvement after binder and resuscitation → urgent angio-embolisation or surgery may be needed**; consider CT and get paediatric trauma specialist advice.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Trauma - Pelvic injury' (Last updated March 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Trauma_-_Pelvic_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Every child with major trauma belongs at a major trauma service — transfer them**, following local transfer guidelines.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Trauma - Pelvic injury' (Last updated March 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Trauma_-_Pelvic_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Unstable fracture: the binder stays on until definitive stabilisation.** If it seems to worsen instability by distracting the fracture (e.g. lateral compression fractures), loosening or removing it may help — **only with orthopaedics and senior oversight.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Trauma - Pelvic injury' (Last updated March 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Trauma_-_Pelvic_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Remove a binder only where resuscitation is possible, and watch for deterioration** — a binder can fully reduce an unstable fracture so it doesn't show on X-ray or CT. **If the child deteriorates, reapply and re-image.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Trauma - Pelvic injury' (Last updated March 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Trauma_-_Pelvic_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Binders cause abrasions and pressure sores — remove at the earliest opportunity when there is no fracture.** With a stable fracture, consult orthopaedics before removal.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Trauma - Pelvic injury' (Last updated March 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Trauma_-_Pelvic_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23
